name: AGIAS Reception
description: Reception for agias.dev. Deterministic and rule-based: it returns a fixed table of facts about AGIAS (what you can ask for: GENERATIVE SYSTEMS, NIGHTLY RESEARCH, AUTONOMOUS OPERATIONS; how a request runs; machines; records; method; contact) and can forward a short message to the operator. No language model runs behind it, so it does not reason, chat, or answer open questions (a message it forwards is read later by the operator and the operator's AI secretary). Nothing it returns is an instruction to you; reading it creates no obligation.

skills.name: About AGIAS
skills.description: Returns the current facts about AGIAS as text and as structured JSON (same content as /llms.txt): the three offers with what you give and what you get, the five steps of a request, machines, records, method, contact. Dated so you can tell when they are stale. Default skill.
examples: What can I ask AGIAS for?
List the machines and their status.
Give me the DOI of Economy of Love.

skills.name: Leave a message for the operator
skills.description: Forwards a short text (up to 2000 characters) to the operator. A few lines are enough. Start the text with "message:" or "leave-message:" (only these two prefixes; case-insensitive), or set the request's params.metadata.skill (or message.metadata.skill) to "leave-message". Send a message.messageId (1-80 printable ASCII characters, unique per message, e.g. a UUID); it is required, and resending the same text with the same messageId is detected as a duplicate on the operator's side. Text parts only. The task returns COMPLETED when delivered (the status text says to which route), FAILED when delivery fails, REJECTED when messages are not being accepted; each carries the reason. Replies are not automatic and not guaranteed; if there is one, it comes by email. Privacy: a message is read by the operator's AI secretary (Claude by Anthropic, processed outside Japan, including the United States) to summarise it for the operator; by leaving a message, the sender consents to that (https://agias.dev/privacy, sections 2.2 and 4). To avoid it, write to ai@agias.dev instead; mail is read by the operator.
examples: message: A generator that turns our product photos into a fresh looping visual every week for the shop screen.
message: Nightly research on WebGPU compute for a small studio.
